The energy a device gives out. A lamp's output is light and heat (input: electrical energy → output: light + heat).
The energy a device needs to work. A fan's input is electrical energy, and its output is movement.
A device gives out useful energy (like light from a bulb) and often some wasted energy too (like heat). A bulb's light is useful; the heat it gives off is wasted.

questions.front: Why does the Moon change shape?
questions.back: It does not really change! We only see the part of the Moon that the Sun is shining on, and that part changes as the Moon orbits the Earth.
The different shapes of the Moon we see from Earth. There are eight main phases, and they repeat every 29 and a half days.
New moon, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full moon, waning gibbous, third (last) quarter, waning crescent.
Waxing means the lit part is growing bigger. Waning means the lit part is getting smaller.

questions.back: When the Moon passes between the Sun and the Earth and blocks some or all of the Sun's light. It happens only at a new moon.

The umbra is the dark, central part of a shadow. The penumbra is the lighter outer part of the shadow.

The Sun's glowing outer layer. You can only see it during a total solar eclipse, when the Moon hides the bright disc of the Sun.
